rules.title: Your caches (~/Library/Caches)
rules.summary: Caches of your apps; safe to clear, apps rebuild them
rules.whatItIs: Per-user caches of macOS and apps: browsers, package managers (Homebrew, pip), Xcode tools, media apps and more.
rules.whyBig: Apps rarely limit their caches; browsers, Homebrew and developer tools often make it several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing important is lost; apps rebuild their caches and may be slower at first. Quit apps first.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete the largest subfolders while the owning apps are closed.

rules.title: Homebrew download cache
rules.summary: Downloaded Homebrew packages; clear with brew cleanup
rules.whatItIs: Bottles and source archives Homebrew downloaded.
rules.whyBig: Old versions stay until 'brew cleanup' runs.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; packages are downloaded again when needed.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'brew cleanup --prune=all'.

rules.title: Your logs
rules.summary: Logs and crash reports of your apps; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files and diagnostic reports of apps you run.
rules.whyBig: Chatty apps and crash reports accumulate.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; you lose troubleshooting history.

rules.title: Xcode DerivedData
rules.summary: Xcode build products and indexes; rebuilt on the next build
rules.whatItIs: Build intermediates, products and code indexes of every project you built in Xcode.
rules.whyBig: Each project and scheme adds builds and indexes; tens of GB is common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build and indexing take longer. Quit Xcode first.

rules.title: Xcode archives
rules.summary: Archived app builds you distributed; needed to symbolicate their crash reports
rules.whatItIs: Archives created by Product > Archive, including the app and its debug symbols (dSYMs).
rules.whyBig: Every archive keeps a full app build with symbols.
rules.ifDeleted: You can no longer re-export those builds or symbolicate crash reports from them unless the symbols are stored elsewhere.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete archives of versions that are no longer in use, from Xcode's Organizer.

rules.title: iOS device support files
rules.summary: Debug symbols copied from connected iPhones; recreated when a device connects
rules.whatItIs: Symbols Xcode copies from each iOS version of devices you connected for debugging.
rules.whyBig: Several GB per iOS version, and old versions stay.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Xcode copies the symbols again (slowly) the next time that device connects.

rules.title: watchOS device support files
rules.summary: Debug symbols copied from Apple Watches; recreated when needed
rules.whatItIs: Symbols Xcode copies from each watchOS version you debugged on.
rules.whyBig: Several GB per version.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Xcode copies them again when needed.

rules.title: iOS Simulator devices
rules.summary: Simulator devices and the apps and data inside them
rules.whatItIs: Each folder is one simulator device with its installed apps and data.
rules.whyBig: Every simulator you booted keeps its data; devices of removed runtimes remain.
rules.ifDeleted: Simulators and their app data are gone; Xcode recreates default devices.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'xcrun simctl delete unavailable' to remove devices whose runtime is gone.

rules.title: iOS Simulator caches
rules.summary: Caches of the iOS Simulator; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Dyld and other caches the Simulator builds for each runtime.
rules.whyBig: Several GB per runtime.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the Simulator rebuilds them (first boot is slower).

rules.title: Simulator runtimes
rules.summary: Installed iOS/watchOS/tvOS/visionOS simulator runtimes
rules.whatItIs: System-wide simulator runtimes that Xcode downloads (stored as disk images and mounted when used).
rules.whyBig: Each runtime is 5-10 GB, and old ones stay after Xcode updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Simulators using a removed runtime no longer start until it is downloaded again.
rules.saferAlternative: List runtimes with 'xcrun simctl runtime list' and delete unused ones with 'xcrun simctl runtime delete <id>', or from Xcode > Settings > Platforms.

rules.title: App sandbox containers
rules.summary: Data of sandboxed apps (including Apple apps); deleting resets the app
rules.whatItIs: Every sandboxed app (Mac App Store apps and many Apple apps) keeps its private data, settings and caches in its own container here.
rules.whyBig: Apps like Docker Desktop, messengers and editors store large data inside their containers.
rules.ifDeleted: The app loses its data and settings; for Apple apps this can include local mail, notes or messages data.
rules.saferAlternative: Clear data from inside each app, or remove the app and its container together.

rules.title: Shared app containers
rules.summary: Data shared between apps from the same developer (Office, Messages, iCloud)
rules.whatItIs: Containers that app groups share: Microsoft Office, Apple apps and app extensions keep shared data here.
rules.whyBig: Office caches, shared databases and media.
rules.ifDeleted: The apps lose shared data and settings.

rules.title: Application Support
rules.summary: App data for your account: databases, libraries, settings, sometimes downloads
rules.whatItIs: Where apps keep their data: databases, game data, plug-ins, profiles, iPhone backups (MobileSync) and more.
rules.whyBig: Browser profiles, iPhone backups, game launchers and creative apps.
rules.ifDeleted: Apps lose their data and settings.
rules.saferAlternative: Check each app's folder.

rules.title: iPhone and iPad backups
rules.summary: Local backups of your iPhone or iPad; manage them in Finder
rules.whatItIs: Full local backups of iOS and iPadOS devices made with Finder (or iTunes on older macOS). Each folder is one device backup.
rules.whyBig: Each backup is roughly the size of the device's data, often tens of GB, and old devices' backups remain.
rules.ifDeleted: The backups are gone; if a device is lost or reset you cannot restore from them.
rules.saferAlternative: In Finder, select the device > Manage Backups to delete old ones.

rules.title: iCloud Drive
rules.summary: iCloud Drive files; evicted files show their size but use little disk
rules.whatItIs: The local copy of iCloud Drive and app documents synced with iCloud.
rules.whyBig: With Optimize Mac Storage, files can be evicted to the cloud, so sizes here can differ from real disk use.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting files here deletes them from iCloud and other devices as well.
rules.saferAlternative: Turn on Optimize Mac Storage in System Settings > Apple Account > iCloud > iCloud Drive.

rules.title: Messages attachments
rules.summary: Photos and files received in Messages
rules.whatItIs: Attachments of conversations in the Messages app.
rules.whyBig: Photos and videos in chats add up over years.
rules.ifDeleted: The attachments disappear from your conversations unless stored in iCloud.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete large attachments from System Settings > General > Storage > Messages.

rules.title: Mail data
rules.summary: Local mail database and downloaded messages of Apple Mail
rules.whatItIs: Apple Mail's local store of messages and attachments.
rules.whyBig: Mailboxes with many attachments grow large.
rules.ifDeleted: Local copies are lost; IMAP mail downloads again, but local-only mailboxes are lost.

rules.title: Photos library
rules.summary: Your Photos library; never edit or delete files inside it by hand
rules.whatItIs: A Photos library package with originals, edits, thumbnails and the database.
rules.whyBig: Originals plus derivatives; with Optimize Mac Storage some originals are only in iCloud.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting files inside corrupts the library; deleting the whole library loses photos not stored in iCloud.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete photos inside the Photos app, and turn on Optimize Mac Storage for iCloud Photos.

rules.title: Trash
rules.summary: Files you moved to the Trash; empty it after checking
rules.whatItIs: Files you deleted in Finder, kept until the Trash is emptied.
rules.whyBig: Deleted files keep their full size until emptied.
rules.ifDeleted: The files can no longer be restored.
rules.saferAlternative: Open the Trash, restore what you need and choose Empty.

rules.title: Docker Desktop disk image
rules.summary: Docker Desktop's disk with all images and containers; prune, do not delete
rules.whatItIs: The sparse disk image in which Docker Desktop stores all images, containers, volumes and build cache.
rules.whyBig: It is a sparse file: Finder may show its maximum size while the real disk use is lower. It grows with pulled images, builds and volumes.
rules.ifDeleted: Every Docker image, container and volume is lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'docker system prune', or lower the disk limit in Docker Desktop > Settings > Resources.

rules.title: macOS system (/System)
rules.summary: macOS itself, on a sealed read-only volume
rules.whatItIs: The macOS operating system on the signed, read-only system volume.
rules.whyBig: Its size changes only with macOS updates.
rules.ifDeleted: It cannot be modified; System Integrity Protection blocks changes.

rules.title: System-wide Library
rules.summary: System-wide app data, plug-ins, launch daemons and fonts
rules.whatItIs: Data shared by all users: app support files, audio plug-ins, fonts, launch daemons and agents, and system-wide caches.
rules.whyBig: Audio libraries, simulator runtimes and app support data.
rules.ifDeleted: Apps and system services that depend on these files break.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove apps with their own uninstallers.

rules.title: System-wide caches
rules.summary: Caches shared by all users; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Caches of system services and apps shared between users.
rules.whyBig: Grows with updates and installed apps.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing important is lost; caches are rebuilt.

rules.title: Applications
rules.summary: Installed apps; move unused ones to the Trash or use their uninstaller
rules.whatItIs: Apps installed for all users. Each .app bundle contains the whole app.
rules.whyBig: Xcode (10+ GB), creative suites and games are the usual large apps.
rules.ifDeleted: The app is removed; its data stays in ~/Library until removed separately.
rules.saferAlternative: Drag the app to the Trash or run its own uninstaller; App Store apps can be deleted from Launchpad.

rules.title: Xcode Command Line Tools
rules.summary: Compilers and developer tools (git, clang) without full Xcode
rules.whatItIs: Apple's command line developer tools: clang, git, make and SDKs.
rules.whyBig: A few GB.
rules.ifDeleted: git, compilers and Homebrew builds stop working until reinstalled with 'xcode-select --install'.

rules.title: Swap and sleep image
rules.summary: macOS swap files and the hibernation sleepimage; managed by the system
rules.whatItIs: Swap files used as virtual memory and the sleepimage that stores memory for hibernation.
rules.whyBig: Swap grows with memory pressure; the sleepimage is sized from RAM.
rules.ifDeleted: The files are in use and protected; deleting them can crash apps or break sleep.
rules.saferAlternative: Reboot to reset swap. The sleepimage depends on the hibernation mode set with pmset.

rules.title: Per-user temporary and cache folders
rules.summary: Temporary files and caches of running apps; reboot to let macOS clean it
rules.whatItIs: macOS's per-user temporary (T) and cache (C) folders, used by every running app and system service.
rules.whyBig: Apps that leave temporary files behind and system caches.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting it while you are logged in can break running apps and system services.
rules.saferAlternative: Restart the Mac; macOS cleans temporary files during boot.

rules.title: Time Machine local snapshots
rules.summary: Local Time Machine snapshots; macOS removes them when space is needed
rules.whatItIs: Snapshots of your startup disk that Time Machine keeps locally between backups.
rules.whyBig: They hold changes since recent backups; macOS deletes them automatically when free space runs low, so they count as 'purgeable'.
rules.ifDeleted: They cannot be deleted as files.
rules.saferAlternative: List them with 'tmutil listlocalsnapshots /' and delete one with 'sudo tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <date>'.

rules.title: Homebrew (Apple silicon)
rules.summary: Homebrew and the packages it installed
rules.whatItIs: Homebrew's prefix on Apple silicon Macs: installed packages (Cellar, Caskroom) and their links.
rules.whyBig: Old package versions stay until 'brew cleanup'.
rules.ifDeleted: Everything installed with Homebrew stops working.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'brew cleanup' and uninstall unused packages with 'brew uninstall'.

rules.title: pnpm store
rules.summary: pnpm's shared package store; hard links make its size look doubled
rules.whatItIs: pnpm keeps one copy of every package version here and hard-links it into projects.
rules.whyBig: Every package version used by any project; hard-linked files are also counted in each node_modules.
rules.ifDeleted: Existing projects keep working; the next install downloads again.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'pnpm store prune'.
